definitions.definition: For each natural r, Y_r=(1/(r! in C)) y^r.

definitions.definition: For each natural i, e_i=(1/(i! in C)) y^i v.

definitions.type: integer-valued family indexed by natural numbers
definitions.definition: For natural j, c_j is the integer cast of Nat.choose(λ.toNat,j). For λ≥0 this is binom(λ,j).

definitions.type: family of complex-linear endomorphisms of V indexed by natural i,j≤λ.toNat
definitions.definition: A_ij=X_(λ.toNat−i) Y_(λ.toNat) X_(λ.toNat) Y_(λ.toNat−j), with the rightmost factor acting first.
D=∏_(t=0)^(λ.toNat) c_t; an empty product is one.
U=V(K)=M⊗_Z K, the balanced tensor product of integer modules. Its K-action is a·(m⊗b)=m⊗(ab).

definitions.type: integer subalgebra of the complex universal enveloping algebra of sl₂(C)
definitions.definition: U_Z is the unital integer subalgebra generated by the elements X_r and Y_r for all natural r, acting on V by the specified representation.

L(K)=(Zx+Zy+Zh)⊗_Z K, equipped, whenever the commutator relations and lattice stability in the original assumptions hold, with their induced commutator bracket and action on U. The bracket normalization is [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=−2y, [x,y]=h, including characteristic 2.

inputs.statement: p is an arbitrary prime, K is an arbitrary field with Char K=p, and λ is an integer with 0≤λ<p.

M⊂V is an arbitrary free abelian subgroup with an integer basis which is also a complex basis of V, and M is stable under the integer enveloping subalgebra generated by all X_r=x^r/r! and Y_r=y^r/r! (r∈N). The induced x,y,h actions on V(K)=M⊗_Z K are the actions in the target.

For i=0,…,λ, the vectors e_i=y^iv/i! form a complex basis of V. They satisfy xe_0=0, xe_i=(λ−i+1)e_(i−1) for 1≤i≤λ, ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for i<λ, ye_λ=0, and he_i=(λ−2i)e_i. For every r≥0, X_r e_i=binom(λ−i+r,r)e_(i−r) if r≤i and zero otherwise; Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) if i+r≤λ and zero otherwise.

output.statement: For i,j∈{0,…,λ}, let E_ij be the complex linear map sending e_j to e_i and every e_k with k≠j to zero, and put c_j=binom(λ,j), A_ij=X_(λ−i)Y_λX_λY_(λ−j), and D=∏_(t=0)^λ c_t. Each A_ij preserves M, A_ij=c_jE_ij, A_ij A_kl=δ_(jk)c_j A_il, and D Id_V=Σ_(i=0)^λ(∏_(t≠i)c_t)A_ii.

binders.type: complex matrix-unit family relative to the basis (e_i); E_ij(e_j)=e_i and E_ij(e_k)=0 for k≠j

locals.declaration: Define E_ij on the N001 basis by E_ij(e_j)=e_i and E_ij(e_k)=0 if k≠j.

argument.text: Use the basis in N001 to define E and set Q=Y_λX_λ. The divided-power formulas give X_λe_k=0 for k<λ and X_λe_λ=e_0, while Y_λe_0=e_λ. Hence Q=E_(λλ). For every i≤λ, X_(λ−i)e_λ=e_i since its coefficient is binom(λ−λ+(λ−i),λ−i)=1; therefore X_(λ−i)Q=E_(iλ). For every j≤λ, QY_(λ−j) kills inputs e_k with k<j because they land below λ, kills inputs with k>j by termination, and sends e_j to binom(λ,λ−j)e_λ=c_j e_λ. Here binom(λ,λ−j)=binom(λ,j), as seen from the identical factorial ratios λ!/[j!(λ−j)!]. Thus QY_(λ−j)=c_jE_(λj).

By D006 and F001, for all i,j in the index set A_ij=X_(λ−i)QY_(λ−j)=c_j E_ij. By H003 every divided power factor in this expression belongs to U_Z and preserves M, and a composition of maps preserving M preserves M. Thus each A_ij preserves M; this uses no assertion that E_ij itself preserves M.

produces.statement: For all 0≤i,j≤λ, A_ij preserves M and A_ij=c_jE_ij.

argument.text: Evaluation on the basis gives E_ijE_kl=δ_(jk)E_il and Σ_i E_ii=Id_V. Using F002, A_ijA_kl=c_jc_lδ_(jk)E_il=δ_(jk)c_j A_il. Also Σ_i(∏_(t≠i)c_t)A_ii=Σ_i(∏_t c_t)E_ii=D Id_V. These use only integer coefficients. Empty products equal one, so the calculation also covers λ=0. Together with F002 these prove every clause of the output statement.

background_notes.justification: Write each u∈V uniquely as Σ_(k=0)^n a_ke_k and set T(u)=Σ_(k=0)^n a_kw_k. Unique basis coordinates ensure the definition is well defined. Coordinate addition and scalar multiplication prove linearity. Any linear map with these images must have this formula, giving uniqueness and equality from basis evaluations.

background_notes.fact: For natural n and 0≤j≤n, binom(n,n−j)=binom(n,j), and binom(n,0)=binom(n,n)=1. For n=λ.toNat these give exactly the endpoint coefficients and c_j used in S001, also after the canonical casts into ℤ and ℂ.

grounds.reason: H001 supplies nonnegative λ, so λ is the integer cast of n=λ.toNat.
D005 defines c_j as the integer cast of Nat.choose(n,j).
S001 restricts i,j to the natural interval 0,…,λ and displays the symmetric factorial quotients.

background_notes.justification: For 0≤j≤n the binomial coefficient has factorial quotient n!/[j!(n−j)!]. Exchanging j and n−j leaves the denominator unchanged; its factorials are positive integers. At j=0 or j=n the quotient equals one. These finite combinatorial identities establish precisely the coefficients used here without any inversion of c_j.
